title: API 580 Training in St. Louis: RBI Exam Prep Online
description: API 580 exam prep for St. Louis-area RBI teams: Wood River and Metro East programmes, Missouri vessel law, PSM and breakout tank rules, self-paced.
h1: API 580 training in St. Louis: self-paced preparation for inspection planners, integrity engineers and inspectors sitting the risk-based inspection exam
html:
API 580 exam prep for risk-based inspection teams around St. Louis

Risk-based inspection decides where an inspection department spends its effort: which vessels, circuits and tanks deserve close attention and with which methods, and which can safely wait. Around St. Louis, most of that planning is done for the Wood River refinery at Roxana and for the pipelines and terminals that surround it, with smaller programmes at chemical plants in the Metro East. The API 580 Risk Based Inspection certification tests whether a candidate understands the principles behind such a programme as API RP 580 describes them.

Atlantis NDT's API 580 course is exam preparation. You work through it online at your own pace and put questions to an instructor whenever something in RP 580 will not settle. There is no Atlantis classroom in St. Louis. API administers the examination, which can be taken at a test centre or by remote proctoring, and issues the certification to candidates who pass.

The examination itself is short beside the inspector codes: 90 multiple-choice questions, of which 80 are scored, in three hours and fifteen minutes, all closed-book. The 2026 Body of Knowledge names a single reference, RP 580's fourth edition of August 2023 with Addendum 1 of March 2025, and says the exam focuses on the most recent edition of that document.

Who sits API 580 in the St. Louis region

The candidates tend to come from a handful of jobs:

  • Certified inspectors. A current API 510, 570 or 653 certificate qualifies you automatically, so refinery and contractor inspectors who already hold one of those often add API 580 when they start contributing to inspection plans.
  • Integrity, reliability and corrosion engineers at the refinery and its contractors. Without an inspector certificate, API asks for education plus petrochemical industry experience gained in the last ten years: one year with a bachelor's degree, two with a two-year degree, three with a high school diploma and five or more with no formal education.
  • Inspection planners and data specialists who maintain the thickness histories, damage mechanism reviews and inspection plans an RBI programme runs on.
  • Chemical plant engineers, for example at the Sauget industrial area, where Afton Chemical makes fuel and lubricant additives. API decides whether a particular chemical plant job counts as petrochemical industry experience, so ask before you count on it.
  • Pipeline and terminal integrity staff around Wood River and Hartford, who meet RBI mostly through the limits federal rules place on it.

RBI after an ownership change

Wood River changed hands recently. Phillips 66's results say it completed the purchase of Cenovus's half of WRB Refining, the partnership that owned the refinery, in October 2025, and EIA's Refinery Capacity Report, compiled as of January 2026, still shows the 50/50 split. Nothing public describes how the refinery's RBI programme was handled through that change, and this page does not guess. What the event usefully illustrates is a theme RP 580 returns to repeatedly: an RBI assessment is only as good as the documented data, assumptions and methodology behind it.

When an organisation, its procedures or its data system changes, the questions an RP 580 reader should ask are predictable. Are the damage mechanism reviews still traceable to the equipment they cover? Did every inspection record survive the move, with its date, method and coverage? Do the risk targets and the risk matrix still mean what they meant before? RP 580 expects the assessment to be revisited when significant changes occur, whether in process conditions, equipment, damage mechanisms, inspection results or the premises of the assessment itself, and it expects the documentation to show why each decision was made. The exam tests that logic in general terms, so candidates who have lived through an integration often find these questions easier than the vocabulary ones.

The exam's ten categories, read through St. Louis equipment

The Body of Knowledge lists ten categories. Here is each one with the local equipment that makes it concrete:

  1. Terms, definitions and acronyms. Probability of failure, consequence of failure, inspection effectiveness and risk itself have exact meanings in RP 580; learn them as written.
  2. Risk assessment. Qualitative, semi-quantitative and quantitative approaches, and when a refinery might use each for different parts of a plant with coking, cracking, hydrocracking and reforming units.
  3. RBI program. Scope, objectives and boundaries, including whether tank fields and offsite piping sit inside the same programme as the process units.
  4. Roles, responsibilities, training and qualifications. The team RP 580 describes: inspection, materials and corrosion, process, operations, and someone who owns the risk decisions.
  5. Data collection. Design, materials, process and inspection data, and what to do when it is incomplete.
  6. Damage mechanisms. Identifying credible mechanisms for each item, from high-temperature sulfidation in crude and coker service to corrosion under insulation on traced lines.
  7. POF. How damage rate, inspection history and inspection effectiveness combine into a likelihood.
  8. COF. What a release would do to people, the environment and the business.
  9. Risk management. Turning a ranking into an inspection plan, mitigation and reassessment dates.
  10. RBI documentation. What has to be recorded so that someone else can audit and repeat the assessment.

Consequence of failure beside the Mississippi

Probability is often where inspectors feel at home; consequence is where St. Louis geography comes in. RP 580 treats consequence broadly, covering harm to people, harm to the environment and the cost of lost production and repairs. The same leak scores very differently depending on the fluid, how much inventory can escape before isolation, and what sits nearby: neighbouring communities, other process units, a river, or the pipelines and terminals that a refinery supplies.

That last point is easy to overlook. Kinder Morgan's Wood River Terminal in Hartford lists Phillips 66 among the pipelines delivering into it, alongside Marathon and Explorer, so an outage at a source can be felt in storage and at truck racks some distance away. Consequence analysis in RP 580 is about understanding those effects well enough to rank equipment sensibly, not about building a perfect model. Expect exam questions that ask which factor would raise or lower a consequence estimate, and answer them from the RP 580 text rather than from a software package you use at work.

Where RBI meets the rulebooks around St. Louis

An RBI result is an engineering basis for an inspection plan. It does not override a law, and three sets of rules shape what it can do here.

OSHA process safety management

Under 29 CFR 1910.119(j), covered processes need a mechanical integrity programme in which inspection and test frequency follows manufacturers' recommendations and good engineering practice, and becomes more frequent if operating experience shows it should. OSHA's 2015 RAGAGEP memorandum, since archived, said employers select the recognised practices their equipment must comply with. It did not name RBI, but many owners use an RP 580 programme as the documented reasoning behind their frequencies.

Missouri and Illinois vessel law

On the Missouri side, section 650.260 of the state's boiler and pressure vessel act calls for a certificate inspection every two years on pressure vessels subject to internal corrosion, leaving the board to set intervals for other vessels and to allow longer ones. An RBI study that supports a longer internal interval therefore does not change the state cycle by itself; the board would have to agree. Illinois runs its own owner-user programme rules, which the Chicago page for API 510 describes.

Pipeline breakout tanks

Atmospheric and low-pressure steel breakout tanks regulated by PHMSA under 49 CFR 195.432 must be inspected to API 653, but the rule excludes API 653's risk-based alternative for setting the internal inspection interval. PHMSA published a proposal in June 2026 that would allow RBI-based internal intervals tied to API 653's fifth edition, capped at 20 years for the initial internal inspection and 25 years after that. It is a proposal, with comments due in August 2026, and at the time of writing it was not a final rule.

A closed-book scenario: inspection history lost in a records migration

Consider an exchanger shell in sour service whose two most recent thickness surveys were not carried across when a plant moved to a new inspection database. The earlier records show a low corrosion rate, and the assessment that last ranked the exchanger gave it credit for those two surveys. A question might ask what the RBI team should do next.

Work it the RP 580 way. An inspection that cannot be shown to have happened, with its method and coverage, cannot earn credit for reducing uncertainty, so the exchanger's probability of failure should be reconsidered without it, or with assumptions that are clearly conservative and documented. The low historical rate is not a reason to keep the old ranking, because the missing surveys are exactly the ones that would reveal any change in the damage rate. The sensible outcomes are to recover the records if they exist, to plan an inspection that closes the gap, and to record the decision. Options that simply carry the previous risk forward, or wait for the next scheduled turnaround without reassessing, are the ones RP 580's logic rules out.

Test centre or remote proctoring from St. Louis

API's programme page says the API 580 exam can now be scheduled either at in-person test centres or through remote proctoring. Prometric lists test centres in and around St. Louis. If you sit remotely, the exam runs on ProProctor, Prometric's remote testing platform, so follow its requirements for the room and the computer. Either way the rules are the same: no references, no notes, and nothing brought in. Exam windows and deadlines are listed on the API exam schedule page.

Studying for API 580 next to a planning or inspection job

Because the exam has one reference, the core task is to read RP 580 slowly and more than once, and to be able to explain each term without looking it up. The self-paced course takes it section by section, with closed-book practice questions after each, and the instructor answers questions such as how RP 580 separates the probability side of risk from the consequence side, or what earns an inspection credit for effectiveness. People who already work in a plan-and-review cycle at the refinery or a contractor usually find that the job supplies examples for every chapter; the effort goes into matching the exam's wording rather than the vocabulary of their own site. The national API 580 training page sets out the full syllabus.

Exam preparation is not an RBI study

Passing API 580 shows understanding of RP 580; it does not train you on a particular RBI software package, and it does not authorise you to approve inspection intervals, which remain with the owner's inspection organisation and its inspector of record. Atlantis also carries out RBI studies remotely for owners who want one; the risk-based inspection page explains that service separately from this course.

Sponsoring API 580 candidates from a St. Louis site

An RBI programme works best when inspectors, engineers and planners share the vocabulary, so sites often sponsor a mixed group. Fees are quoted on request for the group as a whole, and each person still applies to API and sits the examination in their own name.

faq.q: I already hold API 570. Do I still have to apply for API 580?
faq.a: Yes. A current API 510, 570 or 653 certificate means you automatically meet the API 580 eligibility requirement, so you do not need to document petrochemical experience separately, but you still submit an application to API, pay API's fees and sit the examination in your own window. Keep your existing certificate current through the application period, because the automatic route depends on it.

faq.q: Does experience at a Sauget chemical plant count as petrochemical industry experience?
faq.a: It may. API's API 580 requirement is education plus petrochemical industry experience gained within the last ten years, and API is the body that decides whether a particular job meets it. Work on process equipment, inspection planning, corrosion or reliability at a chemical or additives plant is the kind of experience to describe carefully on the application. If in doubt, ask API before you choose a window.

faq.q: Can a Missouri vessel's two-year certificate interval be stretched on the strength of an RBI study?
faq.a: Not by the RBI study alone. Missouri's act sets a two-year certificate inspection for pressure vessels subject to internal corrosion, and it is the board that may allow longer intervals. An RBI assessment can be the engineering case an owner presents, but the statutory cycle applies until the state agrees otherwise. The API 580 exam does not test state law; it tests RP 580.

faq.q: Is API RP 581 on the API 580 exam?
faq.a: The 2026 API 580 Body of Knowledge lists one reference publication, RP 580 in its fourth edition with Addendum 1, and RP 581, the quantitative method, is not among the references. You will meet quantitative RBI as a concept, because RP 580 describes qualitative, semi-quantitative and quantitative approaches, but the exam does not ask you to run RP 581 calculations. Check the Body of Knowledge for your own window in case API changes it.

faq.q: Can I take API 580 from home in St. Louis?
faq.a: API's programme page says the API 580 exam can be scheduled at an in-person test centre or through remote proctoring, which is different from API 510, 570 and 653. If you choose remote proctoring, you need a suitable room and computer that meet Prometric's remote testing rules. The exam stays closed-book either way, with no notes or references allowed, so the preparation is the same.

faq.q: After passing API 580, could I sign off the inspection intervals at a Metro East plant?
faq.a: No. API 580 certifies knowledge of risk-based inspection principles. Who approves an inspection plan and its intervals is set by the owner's programme, the applicable inspection code and, where it applies, state law; at a refinery that is normally the owner's inspection organisation and its authorized inspector. Many API 580 holders contribute to RBI teams and plans, but the certificate does not carry that authority.

faq.q: How is the API 580 certification kept current?
faq.a: The certification lasts three years. You can apply to recertify up to 90 days before it expires, and a 90-day grace period with late fees follows the expiry date. API says employment verification is not currently required to recertify API 580. Put the expiry in your calendar when you pass.

faq.q: Can a refinery planning group enrol for API 580 prep together?
faq.a: Yes. One enquiry can cover inspectors, engineers and planners, and it helps to say which candidates already hold API 510, 570 or 653 and which will apply on education and experience. The quote covers the group. Each person studies the course at their own pace with the instructor available, and each applies to API and sits the closed-book examination separately.
